scenario_reading.120: Splinters of Wrath at the cap. Cached passive text: 'Syndra collects Splinters of Wrath ... stacking up to 120 times' and 'At 120 Splinters of Wrath, Syndra achieves Transcendence, increasing her ability power by 15%.' At 120 every Transcendent bonus (Q 40, W 60, E 80, R 100, P 120) is active.
scenario_reading.leaf: rotation.setup[0] = the first ability cast of the derived opening (setup) sequence.

independent_computation.claim: The first cast of any correct Syndra setup is Q (Dark Sphere). E first is mechanically incoherent and strictly dominated.

step_1_dependency_graph.Q Dark Sphere: in-degree 0 - 'Syndra conjures a Dark Sphere at the target location that appears after a 0.6-second delay ... remains on the ground for 6 seconds.' Nothing must precede it. It is the only repeatable generator of Dark Spheres (R also conjures 3, but R is the payoff, not the setup, and is single-cast per fight in this engine).
step_1_dependency_graph.E Scatter the Weak: consumes a sphere for its payoff - 'Dark Spheres can be knocked back for 950 units ... knocking back enemies they hit over 70 units ... Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds, during which they are also revealed, and dealt Scatter the Weak's damage if they were not damaged by the initial cast.' No sphere on the field => cone damage + knockback only, no stun.
step_1_dependency_graph.W Force of Will: consumes a sphere - 'Syndra telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster within 500 units from the target location'. In a champion-only coupled scenario there are no minions or monsters, so W has nothing to throw until Q has placed a sphere.
step_1_dependency_graph.R Unleashed Power: benefits from pre-placed spheres - 'Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones', and the notes add 'A sphere summoned very shortly before Unleashed Power will be used as one of the spheres that get thrown.'
step_1_dependency_graph.conclusion: Q is the unique zero-in-degree node; W, E's stun branch and R's extra spheres all depend on Q's product. Any topological / dependency-respecting derived order starts with Q.

step_2_timing_arithmetic.inputs_from_cache: Q castTime 'none' (0 s), Q sphere spawn delay 0.6 s; E castTime '0.25' s; E notes 'This ability will cast from wherever the caster is at the end of the cast time.'
step_2_timing_arithmetic.E_first: E at t=0 resolves its wave at t=0.25 s. The earliest a sphere can then exist is 0.25 (E cast) + 0 (Q cast) + 0.6 (spawn delay) = 0.85 s, i.e. 0.6 s after the wave has already passed. Zero spheres are pushed: no 1.25 s stun, and no sphere-carried damage instance.
step_2_timing_arithmetic.Q_first: Q at t=0 costs 0 s of shared timeline (castTime 'none'), sphere exists at t=0.6 s. E started at any t >= 0.6 - 0.25 = 0.35 s has its wave resolve at t >= 0.6 s and pushes the sphere: stun 1.25 s plus the pushed-sphere damage branch.
step_2_timing_arithmetic.cost_of_putting_Q_first: zero - Q occupies no cast time on the shared timeline (math-foundations 1.1: 'each cast occupies its sourced cast time, an ability recasts when its effective cooldown has elapsed and no other cast is in progress'). So no scheduling objective (casts per window, damage per rotation, or CC) can prefer E ahead of Q.

step_3_range_self_defeat.inputs_from_cache: E 'knocks them back for 400 units and up to 800 units away from Syndra based on proximity'; Q targetRange 800; R targetRange 675; W targetRange '925 - 950 - 500' with a 500-unit grab radius.
step_3_range_self_defeat.arithmetic: A target at 400 units hit by an opening E is displaced to between 800 and 1200 units. That is at or beyond Q's 800 cast range and well beyond R's 675 cast range, and outside W's 500-unit grab radius around the target. An E-led setup pushes the target out of the range of every ability that is supposed to follow it.
step_3_range_self_defeat.and_conversely: R's notes state 'Spheres that are being pushed by Scatter the Weak (normally ones that were made late during the push) will not get picked up for Unleashed Power' - a further ordering constraint that only makes sense once Q has placed spheres for E to push.

independent_computation.step_4_transcendent_bonuses_at_120: At the 120-splinter cap the E bonus reads 'Collecting 80 Splinters of Wrath enhances Scatter the Weak to have an increased scatter angle and slow enemies hit by 70% for 1.25 seconds starting after the knock back ends or if the target was hit by a pushed Dark Sphere, after the stun has ended.' The enhanced branch is again phrased around a pushed Dark Sphere already existing, i.e. around Q having been cast first. The 120-splinter capstone itself ('+15% ability power') is a stat buff and is order-neutral, so it cannot be the thing that promotes E to setup[0].

Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 40 Splinters of Wrath causes Syndra to periodically stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2.
Active: Syndra telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster within 500 units from the target location, and holds the target near her for 5 seconds.
Recast: Syndra throws the grabbed target towards the target location ... dealing magic damage to them and nearby enemies once they land.

Active: Syndra propels a wave of force in a cone in the target direction that deals magic damage to enemies hit and knocks them back for 400 units and up to 800 units away from Syndra based on proximity, though not through terrain.

Dark Spheres can be knocked back for 950 units and up to 1200 units away from Syndra based on proximity, knocking back enemies they hit over 70 units, though not through terrain. Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds, during which they are also revealed, and dealt Scatter the Weak's damage if they were not damaged by the initial cast.

Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 80 Splinters of Wrath enhances Scatter the Weak to have an increased scatter angle and slow enemies hit by 70% for 1.25 seconds starting after the knock back ends or if the target was hit by a pushed Dark Sphere, after the stun has ended.
notes: Spheres spawned at close range of the ability are more likely to be hit.

sources_quoted.path: Section 1.1 (Renewal theory for cast + auto timing schedules)
quotes: Ability recasts are scheduled on one shared timeline (the champion has one set of hands): each cast occupies its sourced cast time, an ability recasts when its effective cooldown has elapsed and no other cast is in progress, and a cast counts when it starts within the window (`_schedule_shared_casts`).
the shared-timeline version is the superposition with mutual-exclusion, resolved greedily by cast order
sources_quoted.why: Establishes that ordering is a real modelled quantity and that a zero-cast-time ability (Q, castTime 'none') costs nothing to place first.

quotes: module_slots.modeled: P, Q, Q2, W, E, R
out_of_scope: E/W CC (stun, knockback, slow - utility only)
sources_quoted.why: Confirms the 120-splinter option and the Q2 second-charge slot exist. Note this also means the Q-vs-E ordering cannot be justified by CC modelling either way - the CC is not scored - so nothing in the engine's scope creates a reason to lead with E.

why_the_new_value_fails: E as setup[0] resolves its wave 0.6 s before the earliest possible Dark Sphere exists, so the sphere-knockback branch (the entire point of E in a setup) cannot trigger.
E as setup[0] displaces the target 400-800 units further away, past Q's 800 and R's 675 cast ranges and outside W's 500-unit grab radius, breaking every follow-up cast in the same rotation.
Q costs 0 s of shared timeline (castTime 'none'), so leading with Q is free - there is no scheduling objective under which E-first is even neutral, let alone better.

A cooldown-descending derivation (E 15 s > W 12-8 s > Q 7 s) is the only rule that would produce E, but it would have to place R (120/100/80 s) first, not E, so it does not explain the observed leaf either.
caveat: The golden baseline file, the scenario definition and the engine source were deliberately not read, per the oracle protocol. The computation above is the game-mechanics answer derivable from the cached wiki text and the quoted foundations; it says what setup[0] should be, not what any particular code path currently emits.
